commit_message:
[Stream] Fix O(N²) compile-time scaling in partitionRegionConcurrency (#24958)

When analyzing execution regions where many operations share a common
resource operand, `partitionRegionConcurrencyReference` previously
invoked `tiedOp.hasAnyTiedUses(operand)` inside the `operand.getUsers()`
loop. Because checking whether an operand has tied uses involves
scanning its use sites, repeating this check inside the loop caused
quadratic $O(N^2)$ traversal over the users of that operand.

This change hoists the check out of the loop using the static helper
`IREE::Util::TiedOpInterface::hasAnyTiedUses(operand)` as an early exit.
Inside the loop, it now only checks whether the candidate user
implements `TiedOpInterface`. This eliminates redundant scans and
resolves the compiler performance bottleneck while preserving existing
partitioning semantics.

Fixes #24928

  Signed-off-by: @isa-Lai 
  Assisted-by:  Gemini CLI

Signed-off-by: isa-lai <isabellai1004@gmail.com>

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a98f7ed68e (#24963)

LLVM staging branch: `sm-iree-integrates/llvm-20260925`

Adds a cherry-pick of llvm/llvm-project#226903 to support
minimumnumf/maximumnumf semantics. The new reduction kinds were
introduced in llvm/llvm-project@8306f777. QNaN was chosen as an identity
arg for the new kinds so as to propagate signalling NaNs correctly. As
per the LLVM LangRef:

> Return the other argument if one of the arguments is NaN.


(https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#floating-point-min-max-intrinsics-comparison)

Additionally:
- Update compiler and end-to-end TOSA tests for the strict property
assembly format (llvm/llvm-project@b9da7a34)
- Redeclare LLVM libxml2 and xz Bazel dependencies
(llvm/llvm-project@bd0da2bf7dae, llvm/llvm-project@4989b3b0)
- Regenerate API exports

Assisted-by: Codex

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>
name: Tag candidate release

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Propagate affine QDQ through tensor ops

Move affine quantization through supported reshapes, transposes,

[Bazel] Resolve IREE paths and labels in external consumers

Bzlmod consumers may embed IREE under a different path or repository
name. Resolving IREE-owned targets and bundled sources in the
consumer's workspace can break repository setup and target loading
for the consumer.

The following PR adds the use of Labels(..) so those references
can stay attached to IREE while consumer-provided
dependencies and LLVM tools keep their caller-relative meaning.

commit_message:
[CUDA] Raise the default PTX level for sm_89, sm_120 and sm_121

The CUDA target always passes an explicit PTX level to the NVPTX backend and
only raised the +ptx76 default to 7.8 for sm_89. That is below what the
backend accepts for Blackwell, so `--iree-cuda-target=sm_120` (minimum 8.7)
and `sm_121` (minimum 8.8) failed for every program, and below what the FP8
mma.sync intrinsics selected by default on Ada need, so an f8E4M3FN matmul
on sm_89 failed to select `llvm.nvvm.mma.m16n8k32.row.col.f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32`
(PTX 8.4).

Pick the default per architecture: 8.8 for sm_121, 8.7 for sm_120 and 8.4
for sm_89. An explicit --iree-cuda-target-features still wins.

Fixes #24959

Signed-off-by: Samarth Narang <sn2910@nyu.edu>

commit_message: [PluginAPI] Experimental support for dynamic compiler plugins (#24892) Load experimental compiler plugins at runtime with `--iree-load-plugin` or `IREE_LOAD_PLUGINS`. Validate plugin metadata and registration, and allow embedded compilers to recover from failed dynamic registrations. Use one automatically generated compatibility ID derived from the plugin API headers. This is not a full ABI fingerprint: plugins need matching IREE and LLVM/MLIR revisions, compatible toolchains, and aligned ABI-affecting build settings. An attempt is made to document these requirements and cover loader failures, but it should be considered experimental. commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a98f7ed68e (#24963)

LLVM staging branch: `sm-iree-integrates/llvm-20260925`

Adds a cherry-pick of llvm/llvm-project#226903 to support
minimumnumf/maximumnumf semantics. The new reduction kinds were
introduced in llvm/llvm-project@8306f777. QNaN was chosen as an identity
arg for the new kinds so as to propagate signalling NaNs correctly. As
per the LLVM LangRef:

> Return the other argument if one of the arguments is NaN.


(https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#floating-point-min-max-intrinsics-comparison)

Additionally:
- Update compiler and end-to-end TOSA tests for the strict property
assembly format (llvm/llvm-project@b9da7a34)
- Redeclare LLVM libxml2 and xz Bazel dependencies
(llvm/llvm-project@bd0da2bf7dae, llvm/llvm-project@4989b3b0)
- Regenerate API exports

Assisted-by: Codex

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>
name: linux_x64_gcc

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Report per-call statistics in dispatch rows

A dispatch row only showed the per-iteration total of all calls of a
function, which hides both the cost of one call and how much it varies.
Rows now also report, in seconds, the mean, minimum and maximum duration
of one call and the standard deviation of the per-call mean across
profiled batches.

The mean, minimum and maximum come from the statistics rows. The
deviation needs one sample per batch, so the profiling pass reads the
rows after each flushed batch. A forwarding sink serializes those reads
with producer writes, which the statistics sink does not synchronize.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[iree-benchmark-module] Report per-call statistics in dispatch rows

A dispatch row only showed the per-iteration total of all calls of a
function, which hides both the cost of one call and how much it varies.
Rows now also report, in seconds, the mean, minimum and maximum duration
of one call and the standard deviation of the per-call mean across
profiled batches.

The mean, minimum and maximum come from the statistics rows. The
deviation needs one sample per batch, so the profiling pass reads the
rows after each flushed batch. A forwarding sink serializes those reads
with producer writes, which the statistics sink does not synchronize.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: Test ONNX / test_onnx_models :: cpu_llvm_task

commit_message:
[Stream] Fix O(N²) compile-time scaling in partitionRegionConcurrency (#24958)

When analyzing execution regions where many operations share a common
resource operand, `partitionRegionConcurrencyReference` previously
invoked `tiedOp.hasAnyTiedUses(operand)` inside the `operand.getUsers()`
loop. Because checking whether an operand has tied uses involves
scanning its use sites, repeating this check inside the loop caused
quadratic $O(N^2)$ traversal over the users of that operand.

This change hoists the check out of the loop using the static helper
`IREE::Util::TiedOpInterface::hasAnyTiedUses(operand)` as an early exit.
Inside the loop, it now only checks whether the candidate user
implements `TiedOpInterface`. This eliminates redundant scans and
resolves the compiler performance bottleneck while preserving existing
partitioning semantics.

Fixes #24928

  Signed-off-by: @isa-Lai 
  Assisted-by:  Gemini CLI

Signed-off-by: isa-lai <isabellai1004@gmail.com>
name: windows :: Build py-compiler-pkg Package

resource operand, `partitionRegionConcurrencyReference` previously
invoked `tiedOp.hasAnyTiedUses(operand)` inside the `operand.getUsers()`
loop. Because checking whether an operand has tied uses involves
scanning its use sites, repeating this check inside the loop caused
quadratic $O(N^2)$ traversal over the users of that operand.

This change hoists the check out of the loop using the static helper
`IREE::Util::TiedOpInterface::hasAnyTiedUses(operand)` as an early exit.
Inside the loop, it now only checks whether the candidate user
implements `TiedOpInterface`. This eliminates redundant scans and
resolves the compiler performance bottleneck while preserving existing
partitioning semantics.

Fixes #24928

  Assisted-by:  Gemini CLI

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Propagate affine QDQ through tensor ops

Move affine quantization through supported reshapes and padding, fuse
consuming transposes into dequantize, and run propagation before integer
QDQ rewriting so contractions consume dequantize results directly.

Add a pattern that fuses a transpose into its single-use dequantize by
permuting the dequantize's output map, the same map update the generic
producer fusion applies. The integer contraction rewrite already reads
through permuted dequantize maps, so no transpose is materialized on
either side. The QDQ propagation pass uses it together with generic
transpose specialization, restricted to transposes of dequantized
values. The general transpose propagation pass also runs it while
bubbling.

[GlobalOptimization] Propagate affine QDQ through tensor ops

Move affine quantization through supported reshapes and padding, fuse
consuming transposes into dequantize, and run propagation before integer
QDQ rewriting so contractions consume dequantize results directly.

Add a pattern that fuses a transpose into its single-use dequantize by
permuting the dequantize's output map, the same map update the generic
producer fusion applies. The integer contraction rewrite already reads
through permuted dequantize maps, so no transpose is materialized on
either side. The QDQ propagation pass uses it together with generic
transpose specialization, restricted to transposes of dequantized
values. The general transpose propagation pass also runs it while
bubbling.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Bindings][Compiler] Add Bazel support for Python bindings

IREE's compiler Python support is available through CMake, but its generated
dialect bindings, native extensions and compiler tool wrappers are not exposed
as Bazel targets. Downstream projects using Bazel therefore need to maintain
their own build definitions to package Python bindings that match the compiler
they build.

Providing these targets upstream lets consumers build Python compiler packages
against their chosen IREE revision and keeps the binding definitions alongside
the sources they describe. The bindings use `IREECompiler`'s shared C API so
Python code can inspect and construct IR, then invoke the compiler using the
same MLIR implementation. Consumers retain control of package and wheel assembly.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Propagate affine QDQ through tensor ops

Move affine quantization through supported reshapes and padding, fuse
consuming transposes into dequantize, and run propagation before integer
QDQ rewriting so contractions consume dequantize results directly.

Add a pattern that fuses a transpose into its single-use dequantize by
permuting the dequantize's output map, the same map update the generic
producer fusion applies. The integer contraction rewrite already reads
through permuted dequantize maps, so no transpose is materialized on
either side. The QDQ propagation pass uses it together with generic
transpose specialization, restricted to transposes of dequantized
values. The general transpose propagation pass also runs it while
bubbling.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

consuming transposes into dequantize, and run propagation before integer
QDQ rewriting so contractions consume dequantize results directly.

producer fusion applies. The integer contraction rewrite already reads

transpose specialization, restricted to transposes of dequantized

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Expose transpose propagation patterns

Move the transpose propagation patterns out of PropagateLinalgTranspose
into TransposePropagationPatterns so other passes can reuse them. Each
pattern is exposed through its own populate function, and the pattern
classes stay private to the implementation file. Generic transpose
specialization is exposed both as a function, which the pass keeps
applying with its original walk, and as a pattern for greedy callers.

Patterns no longer depend on Flow. Scope and profitability decisions
come from a ControlTransposePropagationFn. The patterns call it once,
after the structural match, with the use edge that the transpose moves
across. The pass supplies the previous policy: stay outside of
dispatches, keep sunk extract_slice ops mappable to Flow, and restrict
reshape propagation at graph edges. Named-op generalization and
convolution support stay pattern options because they describe what
the rewrite can handle safely.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Propagate affine QDQ through tensor ops

Move affine quantization through supported reshapes, transposes,
and padding, and run propagation before integer QDQ rewriting so
contractions consume dequantize results directly.

Add a pattern that bubbles a transpose above its single-use
dequantize so the transpose operates on the quantized values. The
QDQ propagation pass uses it together with generic transpose
specialization, restricted to transposes of dequantized values. The
general transpose propagation pass also runs it while bubbling.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Expose transpose propagation patterns

Move the transpose propagation patterns out of PropagateLinalgTranspose
into TransposePropagationPatterns so other passes can reuse them. Each
pattern is exposed through its own populate function, and the pattern
classes stay private to the implementation file. Generic transpose
specialization is exposed both as a function, which the pass keeps
applying with its original walk, and as a pattern for greedy callers.

Patterns no longer depend on Flow. Scope and profitability decisions
come from a ControlTransposePropagationFn. The patterns call it once,
after the structural match, with the use edge that the transpose moves
across. The pass supplies the previous policy: stay outside of
dispatches, keep sunk extract_slice ops mappable to Flow, and restrict
reshape propagation at graph edges. Named-op generalization and
convolution support stay pattern options because they describe what
the rewrite can handle safely.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Propagate affine QDQ through tensor ops

Move affine quantization through supported reshapes, transposes,
and padding, and run propagation before integer QDQ rewriting so
contractions consume dequantize results directly.

Add a pattern that bubbles a transpose above its single-use
dequantize so the transpose operates on the quantized values. The
QDQ propagation pass uses it together with generic transpose
specialization, restricted to transposes of dequantized values. The
general transpose propagation pass also runs it while bubbling.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Expose transpose propagation patterns

Move the transpose propagation patterns out of PropagateLinalgTranspose
into TransposePropagationPatterns so other passes can reuse them. Each
pattern is exposed through its own populate function, and the pattern
classes stay private to the implementation file. Generic transpose
specialization is exposed both as a function, which the pass keeps
applying with its original walk, and as a pattern for greedy callers.

Patterns no longer depend on Flow. Scope and profitability decisions
come from a ControlTransposePropagationFn. The patterns call it once,
after the structural match, with the use edge that the transpose moves
across. The pass supplies the previous policy: stay outside of
dispatches, keep sunk extract_slice ops mappable to Flow, and restrict
reshape propagation at graph edges. Named-op generalization and
convolution support stay pattern options because they describe what
the rewrite can handle safely.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: Analyze (actions)

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a98f7ed68e (#24963)

LLVM staging branch: `sm-iree-integrates/llvm-20260925`

Adds a cherry-pick of llvm/llvm-project#226903 to support
minimumnumf/maximumnumf semantics. The new reduction kinds were
introduced in llvm/llvm-project@8306f777. QNaN was chosen as an identity
arg for the new kinds so as to propagate signalling NaNs correctly. As
per the LLVM LangRef:

> Return the other argument if one of the arguments is NaN.


(https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#floating-point-min-max-intrinsics-comparison)

Additionally:
- Update compiler and end-to-end TOSA tests for the strict property
assembly format (llvm/llvm-project@b9da7a34)
- Redeclare LLVM libxml2 and xz Bazel dependencies
(llvm/llvm-project@bd0da2bf7dae, llvm/llvm-project@4989b3b0)
- Regenerate API exports

Assisted-by: Codex

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>
name: macos_arm64_clang

assembly format (llvm/llvm-project@b9da7a34)

(llvm/llvm-project@bd0da2bf7dae, llvm/llvm-project@4989b3b0)

commit_message: [PluginAPI] Experimental support for dynamic compiler plugins (#24892) Load experimental compiler plugins at runtime with `--iree-load-plugin` or `IREE_LOAD_PLUGINS`. Validate plugin metadata and registration, and allow embedded compilers to recover from failed dynamic registrations. Use one automatically generated compatibility ID derived from the plugin API headers. This is not a full ABI fingerprint: plugins need matching IREE and LLVM/MLIR revisions, compatible toolchains, and aligned ABI-affecting build settings. An attempt is made to document these requirements and cover loader failures, but it should be considered experimental. commit_message:
[Bazel] Resolve IREE paths and labels in external consumers

Bzlmod consumers may embed IREE under a different path or repository
name. Resolving IREE-owned targets and bundled sources in the
consumer's workspace can break repository setup and target loading
for the consumer.

The following PR adds the use of Labels(..) so those references
can stay attached to IREE while consumer-provided
dependencies and LLVM tools keep their caller-relative meaning.

Assisted-by: GPT-Astra-6

commit_message:
[Bazel] Resolve IREE paths and labels in external consumers

Bzlmod consumers may embed IREE under a different path or repository
name. Resolving IREE-owned targets and bundled sources in the
consumer's workspace can break repository setup and target loading
for the consumer.

The following PR adds the use of Labels(..) so those references
can stay attached to IREE while consumer-provided
dependencies and LLVM tools keep their caller-relative meaning.

Assisted-by: GPT-Astra-6
